title: Private deployments: VPC & on‑prem deployment, packaging, day‑2 ops, and upgrade/rollback guide
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical deployment and operations reference for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC-hosted and on-prem). It consolidates: reference architectures, on‑prem packaging requirements, Day‑2 operational runbooks, and safe upgrade & rollback procedures. Use this guide for customer engagements, SOW scoping, and internal delivery playbooks.

Scope

- Platforms: AWS/Azure/GCP VPC deployments and air‑gapped on‑prem installations
- Components: control plane (optional customer-managed), data plane (inference workers), storage (object & block), networking, KMS/HSM, and telemetry/observability stack
- Audience: Solutions Engineering, Private Deployments Delivery, SRE, Security, and Customer Infrastructure teams

1) Reference architectures (summary)

High‑level patterns:

- Small proof-of-concept (PoC): single-region VPC, 1 control-plane node, 2–4 inference workers (NVIDIA A10 / A5000), managed Postgres for metadata, object store (S3-compatible).
- Production VPC (multi-az): HA control plane (3 nodes), autoscaled inference pool with reserved capacity, cross-AZ object store, private NATs for outbound updates, and cross-account IAM roles where required.
- On‑prem (air‑gapped): customer-provided metal nodes with isolated management network, local object store (MinIO), and optional KMS appliance (HSM).

Architecture checklist (required items)

| Area | Minimum requirement | Recommended / Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Network | Private VPC with dedicated subnets for control & data plane | Route tables with no public subnets for data nodes; control plane may require outbound to Redwood control plane (unless fully private) |
| Compute | 1 control-plane (min) + inference workers sized to QPS & latency targets | GPU: A10/A100 depending on model; reserve capacity for predictable throughput |
| Storage | S3-compatible object store; Postgres 14 for metadata | For on‑prem use MinIO 2025+ and daily backups to removable media |
| Identity | Customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest | HSM recommended for regulated customers |
| Observability | Prometheus + Grafana, log aggregation to secure storage | Trace retention policy: 30d default; metrics at 1m resolution |

2) On‑prem packaging and preflight requirements

Preflight checklist (run with customer prior to install):

- Inventory: list of hostnames, IPs, GPU types, RAID/storage capacities, and rack/cabinet info.
- Network: management VLAN, data VLAN, allowed CIDR for control-plane access, proxy/egress rules (if any).
- Credentials: service account for orchestration, SSH key for install, KMS/HSM operator contacts.
- Capacity planning: expected peak RPS, average sequence length, model family(s) and sizes (FP32/INT8/quantized).

Packaging notes:

- Delivery artifacts: 
  - Installation container image bundle with versioned tags (redwood/private-deploy:2026.03.15),
  - Helm charts for k8s installs (with overlays for air‑gapped),
  - RPM/DEB packages for supported distros for housekeeping agents.
- Air‑gap method: signed tarball containing images + Helm charts + preseeded registry snapshot; installation uses local registry (Harbor) or registry mirror.

3) Deployment procedure (VPC / on‑prem canonical flow)

High-level steps:

1. Validate preflight checklist and sign customer SOW.
2. Prepare network constructs (VPC, subnets, route tables, NACLs) and allocate IP ranges.
3. Provision base compute & storage resources. For AWS: EC2 instances with GPU AMIs; create EBS volumes and attach; create IAM roles and KMS keys.
4. Install control plane: deploy Postgres, object store endpoints, and control-plane components (Helm charts).
5. Register inference workers and verify GPU drivers + CUDA / ROCm versions.
6. Deploy observability stack and run synthetic traffic to validate latency/SLOs.
7. Run security hardening checklist and final acceptance tests.

Example commands (k8s Helm install):

kubectl create namespace redwood-control
helm repo add redwood https://charts.redwood.ai/stable
helm upgrade --install redwood-control redwood/control-plane --namespace redwood-control \
  --set image.tag=2026.03.15 --values values-production.yaml

4) Day‑2 operational runbooks (common procedures)

Standard operating runbooks (short versions):

- Scaling inference workers (manual):
  1. Assess current utilization via Grafana dashboards (model QPS, GPU utilization > 70% indicates need).
  2. Update autoscaling group or k8s HPA: kubectl scale deployment redwood-worker --replicas=8
  3. Monitor KV cache warmup and cold-start latency for 30m.

- Certificate rotation:
  1. Generate new cert in KMS/HSM.
  2. Deploy to control-plane and data-plane via rolling restart (maxUnavailable=1).
  3. Verify TLS handshake to internal endpoints and update clients if necessary.

- Backup & restore of metadata DB (Postgres):
  - Daily logical backups to object store (pg_dump), weekly full physical backups. Restore procedure documented in the DB runbook.

- Incident triage (short):
  1. Identify symptom: increased latency, 5xx errors, or rate limiter alerts.
  2. Check control-plane health endpoints (/healthz), orchestration logs, and worker metrics.
  3. If caused by model incompatibility, failover to fallback model version per routing policy.
  4. Engage escalation contacts if >30 minutes to remediation.

5) Upgrade & rollback procedures (safe path)

Goals: zero data loss, predictable rollback, and minimal customer-facing downtime.

Pre-upgrade:

- Create full backups (metadata DB + object-store manifest).
- Verify test-synthetic canary suite passes in staging with the target version.
- Communicate maintenance window with customers and PSO team.

Canary upgrade steps (recommended):

1. Deploy control-plane patch to the canary subset (1 of 3 control-plane nodes).
2. Monitor control-plane metrics and leader-election stability for 10 minutes.
3. Rollout model-serving binaries to a single worker pool; route 5% of traffic via routing policy.
4. Observe latencies, error rates, and quality regression checks for 30–60 minutes.
5. If stable, proceed in geometric progression (5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%).

Rollback checklist (if canary fails):

- Abort rollout and route traffic to previous model/version.
- Re-deploy previous container tag: helm rollback redwood-control <revision>
- Restore metadata snapshot if schema migration caused failure.
- Postmortem within 72 hours required.

6) Customer requirements library (minimums & asks to collect)

Collect and validate the following before scheduling physical delivery: 

- Contact and escalation list (names, phone, pager, emails)
- Network CIDR blocks, proxy/egress policy, and gateway ACLs
- Hardware inventory: GPU model, driver versions, CPU, memory, local disk sizes
- Compliance constraints: required encryption levels, audit logging retention, required certifications (e.g., SOC2, FedRAMP)
- Operational preferences: maintenance windows, RTO/RPO, monitoring endpoints to which logs/metrics should be forwarded

Minimum sizing table (guideline)

| Use-case | Min GPUs | Typical fleet for 100 QPS | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Development / PoC | 1 x A10 | 2 workers | Lower memory models acceptable |
| Production latency critical | 4 x A100 | 8–16 workers | Pin model shards; prefer reserved capacity |
| Batch/Throughput | 2 x A100 | Autoscale with larger queue depth | Use batching & KV cache aggressively |

7) Ownership, SLAs & notifications

- Delivery owner: Private Deployments Delivery Lead (primary contact).
- Operations owner: Customer’s infra team + Redwood SRE on-call.
- SLOs (example): 99th‑percentile request latency < 600ms for short-text models; 99.9% control-plane availability monthly.

8) Troubleshooting appendix (common failure modes)

- GPU driver mismatch: check nvidia-smi and container runtime logs; ensure CUDA toolkit version matches package matrix in packaging notes.
- KV cache warming slow: verify KV cache shard affinity and consider pre-warm job (run prewarm tool included in image bundle).
- Object-store permission denied: validate IAM roles and bucket policies; for on‑prem check MinIO policy and service account credentials.

9) Links & artifacts

- Helm charts: https://charts.redwood.ai/stable
- Packaging artifacts and signed bundles: s3://redwood-private-delivery/artifacts/2026.03.15/
- Day‑2 runbook quick commands: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-deployment-runbook-2028-03-01.json

  replicas: 3
  image:
    repository: registry.redwood.ai/redwood/control-plane
    tag: 2026.03.15

  defaultReplicas: 4
  gpuType: A10
  resources:
    cpu: 8
    memory: 64Gi
